STEP 1 - Scene: An airline-style meal tray with a plate of tortellini in tomato sauce, a small chocolate/wafer cone wrapped in foil (Dumbo-style cone), and a glass of water. Photographed from a high oblique angle, roughly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white oval plate is about 20 cm across its long axis (similar to a side plate). Area ≈ 3.14 × (10)² ≈ 314 cm² for a round equivalent; the oval is somewhat smaller in effective area, so use ~280 cm². The foil cone is about 12 cm long and serves as a secondary reference.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) cheese tortellini in tomato sauce, (b) tomato sauce (included in the pasta item), (c) foil-wrapped chocolate/wafer cone (not eaten here as a food portion estimate beyond its packaged weight), (d) water in glass (not counted as food energy).

STEP 4 - Area: Tortellini cover about 45% of the plate area visible (roughly 125 cm² of the oval).

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile height is about 2 cm on average. 125 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 250 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Pasta with sauce at ~0.8–0.9 g/ml bulk density → 250 × 0.85 ≈ 210 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Filled tortellini in tomato sauce ≈ 150 kcal/100 g (cooked). 210 g × 1.5 ≈ 315 kcal. The wafer cone (~15 g, ~500 kcal/100 g) adds ≈ 75 kcal if eaten; it is a visible item, so include it.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A plate about half covered with tortellini in sauce, about 200 g, is plausible for an airline portion. Total ≈ 225 g, ≈ 390 kcal. Water is excluded from energy (~0 kcal).
